title: Isomorphism of the degree-zero cycle factor
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $G$ an abelian sheaf on its small étale site [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], and $s:G[0]\to I^\bullet$ a quasi-isomorphism with $I^\bullet$ K-injective [def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions]. Write $\Gamma(T,-)$ for global sections and $Z^0$ for the kernel of the degree-zero differential. If $z:\Gamma(T,G)\to Z^0(\Gamma(T,I^\bullet))$ satisfies $i\circ z=\Gamma(T,s^0)$, where $i$ is the inclusion of cycles, then $\pi\circ z:\Gamma(T,G)\to H^0(\Gamma(T,I^\bullet))$ is an isomorphism, where $\pi$ is the homology projection [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology].

source.place: Lemma Tag 05TD, proof of (3), with a nonnegative injective resolution (Tag 013K) and transport by a homotopy equivalence to the given K-injective resolution.

proof.text: The category of abelian etale sheaves is Grothendieck abelian, hence has enough injectives. Choose its ordinary natural-number-indexed injective resolution R of G and extend by zero to integers. The incoming differential at degree zero vanishes in both G[0] and R. Global sections are additive and preserve finite limits; Functor.preservesLeftHomology_of_zero_f and ShortComplex.quasiIso_map_of_preservesLeftHomology therefore show that H^0(Gamma(R.ι')) is an isomorphism. This implements the left-exact degree-zero comparison without computing an explicit kernel comparison.

R is bounded below and termwise injective, hence K-injective. By the bijection from homotopy-category maps to derived-category maps into I, lift Q(s) Q(R.ι')^{-1} to a chain map a : R -> I. Naturality of quotientCompQhIso and injectivity of that bijection give a homotopy R.ι' ≫ a ∼ s. Its image Q(a) is invertible, so a is a quasi-isomorphism; between the two K-injective complexes it is a homotopy equivalence.

Apply Gamma to this homotopy equivalence and the augmentation homotopy. The homotopy equivalence induces an isomorphism H^0(Gamma(a)); homotopy invariance and composition of homology maps identify H^0(Gamma(s)) with H^0(Gamma(R.ι')) ≫ H^0(Gamma(a)), hence it is an isomorphism.

In the Gamma-image of G[0], the cycle inclusion and homology projection in degree zero are isomorphisms because both adjacent differentials are zero. Set c = Gamma(singleObjXSelf.inv) ≫ iCycles^{-1}. Cancel the monic cycle inclusion using hz to identify z with c ≫ cyclesMap(Gamma(s)). Naturality of homologyπ then gives z ≫ homologyπ = c ≫ homologyπ ≫ H^0(Gamma(s)), a composite of isomorphisms.

blueprint_update.statement: Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $G$ an abelian sheaf on its small étale site, and $s:G[0]\to I^\bullet$ a quasi-isomorphism with $I^\bullet$ K-injective [def-sp-kinjective-bridge]. Write $\Gamma(T,-)$ for global sections and $Z^0$ for the kernel of the degree-zero differential. If $z:\Gamma(T,G)\to Z^0(\Gamma(T,I^\bullet))$ satisfies $i\circ z=\Gamma(T,s^0)$, where $i$ is the inclusion of cycles, then $\pi\circ z:\Gamma(T,G)\to H^0(\Gamma(T,I^\bullet))$ is an isomorphism, where $\pi$ is the homology projection [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology].

proof.text: The category of abelian étale sheaves is Grothendieck abelian, hence has enough injectives ([lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives]). Choose an injective resolution $R$ of $G$ in nonnegative degrees, extended by zero to all integer degrees. The incoming differential at degree zero vanishes in both $G[0]$ and $R$. Global sections are additive and left exact, and the incoming differentials vanish, so global sections preserve the homology in degree zero; therefore $H^0$ of $\Gamma(T,-)$ of the augmentation $\varepsilon\colon G[0]\to R$ is an isomorphism.

$R$ is bounded below and termwise injective, hence K-injective. Maps into the K-injective complex $I^\bullet$ in the derived category are maps in the homotopy category, so $Q(s)\,Q(\varepsilon)^{-1}$, where $Q$ is the localization functor, lifts to a chain map $a\colon R\to I^\bullet$, and $a\circ\varepsilon$ is homotopic to $s$. Its image $Q(a)$ is invertible, so $a$ is a quasi-isomorphism; between the two K-injective complexes it is a homotopy equivalence.

Apply $\Gamma(T,-)$ to this homotopy equivalence and to the homotopy $a\circ\varepsilon\simeq s$. The homotopy equivalence induces an isomorphism $H^0(\Gamma(T,a))$; homotopy invariance and functoriality of homology identify $H^0(\Gamma(T,s))$ with $H^0(\Gamma(T,a))\circ H^0(\Gamma(T,\varepsilon))$, hence it is an isomorphism.

In $\Gamma(T,G[0])$, the inclusion of cycles and the homology projection in degree zero are isomorphisms because both adjacent differentials are zero. Let $c$ be the identification of $\Gamma(T,G)$ with the degree-zero cycles of $\Gamma(T,G[0])$. Cancelling the monomorphism $i$, the hypothesis $i\circ z=\Gamma(T,s^0)$ identifies $z$ with $c$ followed by the map induced by $\Gamma(T,s)$ on degree-zero cycles. Naturality of the homology projection then writes $\pi\circ z$ as $c$, followed by the homology projection of $\Gamma(T,G[0])$ and by $H^0(\Gamma(T,s))$, a composite of isomorphisms.
